---
title: "Normalized % Resistance vs updated stall fraction and meta p-value"
output: html_notebook
---

## Overview

Two inputs are merged here:

1. `cy5_bandquant_plot_20261105_pvalues.xlsx` — the in vitro Cy5 band
   quantification (% resistance, 2 replicates per organism). This is the only
   source of resistance values.
2. `261019_re-run_viromelib_orderedRef.peaks_annotated_known6cm.csv` — the
   updated re-run. All stall-fraction and p-value columns come from here,
   replacing the stale `mean sf` column and the hand-computed Fisher p-value
   used in the previous version of this notebook.

Key points about the merge:

- The full `peak_id` string cannot be used as the join key. Two tile windows
  changed between runs (`orsay` `|93|0-196` -> `|93|0-189`, `pvyv`
  `|188|160-356` -> `|188|160-350`), so a `peak_id` join silently drops those
  two organisms. The stable key is `peak_position_id` (the `peak_id` with the
  trailing `|start-end` window removed) plus `tile_id`.
- `meta_pvalue` from the re-run replaces the Fisher-combined p-value. The
  re-run already combines the three replicates, so combining them again by
  hand is both redundant and less correct.

## Setup

```{r setup, message=FALSE, warning=FALSE}
## install.packages(c("ggplot2","dplyr","ggrepel","readxl","svglite"))  # run once if needed
library(ggplot2)
library(dplyr)
library(ggrepel)
library(readxl)
library(svglite)
```

## 1. Load the Cy5 quantification

```{r load-cy5}
cy5_file <- "cy5_bandquant_plot_20261105_pvalues.xlsx"

cy5 <- read_excel(cy5_file)

# The sheet carries trailing empty spacer columns (Column1..Column7) where the
# old sf / p-value columns were deleted. Keep only the columns we need.
cy5 <- cy5 %>%
  select(
    replicate,
    Organism,
    Accession,
    peak_id,
    tile_id,
    perc_resistance = `Perc. Resistance`
  ) %>%
  mutate(
    replicate = factor(replicate),
    # strip the trailing "|<start>-<end>" window to get peak_position_id
    peak_position_id = sub("\\|[^|]*$", "", peak_id)
  )

cy5
```

## 2. Load the updated peaks table

The re-run file is ~18 MB and ~80 columns wide; we read it once and keep only
the columns used below.

```{r load-peaks}
peaks_file <- "261019_re-run_viromelib_orderedRef.peaks_annotated_known6cm.csv"

peaks_all <- read.csv(peaks_file, stringsAsFactors = FALSE)

peaks <- peaks_all %>%
  select(
    peak_position_id,
    tile_id,
    peak_id_new = peak_id,
    accession,
    species,
    meta_pvalue,
    meta_qvalue,
    mean_treated_sf,
    median_treated_sf,
    stall_site_rank,
    n_reps_passing,
    fail_reasons,
    any_hit,
    treated_sf_R1, treated_sf_R2, treated_sf_R3,
    pvalue_R1, pvalue_R2, pvalue_R3
  )

nrow(peaks_all)
```

## 3. Merge and verify

```{r merge}
merged <- cy5 %>%
  left_join(peaks, by = c("peak_position_id", "tile_id"))

# Fail loudly rather than plotting a silently incomplete figure.
unmatched <- merged %>% filter(is.na(meta_pvalue))
if (nrow(unmatched) > 0) {
  print(unmatched %>% select(Organism, peak_id, tile_id, peak_position_id))
  stop("Some Cy5 rows did not match a peak in the re-run file (see above).")
}

merged %>%
  select(replicate, Organism, species, tile_id,
         mean_treated_sf, meta_pvalue, stall_site_rank, n_reps_passing)
```

```{r write-merged}
write.csv(merged, "merged_cy5_peaks_20261105.csv", row.names = FALSE)
```

## 4. Normalize % resistance

Normalization is anchored to Zika within each replicate, matching how the old
`Norm. Perc. Resistance` column was computed (Zika = 1.0 in both replicates).
The anchor is set explicitly so it is visible and changeable.

```{r normalize}
anchor_organism <- "zikv"

merged <- merged %>%
  group_by(replicate) %>%
  mutate(
    anchor_value = perc_resistance[Organism == anchor_organism][1],
    norm_perc_resistance = perc_resistance / anchor_value
  ) %>%
  ungroup()

merged %>% select(replicate, Organism, perc_resistance, norm_perc_resistance)
```

## 5. Per-organism summary

- `mean_treated_sf` / `sd_sf` — updated mean stall fraction and the SD of its
  three replicates (horizontal error bars on the mean-sf plot)
- `median_treated_sf` — median stall fraction. Not plotted; see 8a and 8b.
- `mad_sf` / `half_range_sf` — alternative spread statistics, tabled in 8c to
  document why error bars use SD.
- `neg_log10_meta_p` — `-log10(meta_pvalue)` from the re-run; higher = more
  significant. This is what the sf plots are colored by, so every sf panel
  carries the p-value information alongside the sf variance.
- `neg_log10_fisher_p` — the three per-replicate p-values recombined by
  Fisher's method, as the old notebook did. Kept only as a cross-check against
  `meta_pvalue`; the re-run's own combination is the one to use.
- `sd_neg_log10_p` — SD of the three per-replicate `-log10(p)` values
  (horizontal error bars on the meta-p plot). This is a spread across the
  individual replicate tests, not an uncertainty on `meta_pvalue` itself.
- `mean_resist` / `sd_resist` — mean and SD of the 2 Cy5 resistance
  replicates (vertical error bars on every plot)
- `point_label` — organism name and genome accession, used for the on-plot
  labels

```{r summarize}
fisher_combine <- function(p) {
  p <- p[!is.na(p)]
  k <- length(p)
  if (k == 0) return(NA_real_)
  pchisq(-2 * sum(log(p)), df = 2 * k, lower.tail = FALSE)
}

# sf and p-values are properties of the peak, identical across the two
# resistance replicate rows, so take one copy per organism.
peak_level <- merged %>%
  distinct(Organism, .keep_all = TRUE) %>%
  rowwise() %>%
  mutate(
    sd_sf              = sd(c(treated_sf_R1, treated_sf_R2, treated_sf_R3)),
    mad_sf             = mad(c(treated_sf_R1, treated_sf_R2, treated_sf_R3)),
    half_range_sf      = diff(range(c(treated_sf_R1, treated_sf_R2,
                                      treated_sf_R3))) / 2,
    neg_log10_meta_p   = -log10(meta_pvalue),
    sd_neg_log10_p     = sd(-log10(c(pvalue_R1, pvalue_R2, pvalue_R3))),
    fisher_p           = fisher_combine(c(pvalue_R1, pvalue_R2, pvalue_R3)),
    neg_log10_fisher_p = -log10(fisher_p)
  ) %>%
  ungroup() %>%
  mutate(
    # "NC_035889.1|10329-10808_inferred_3UTR" -> "NC_035889.1"
    genome      = sub("\\|.*$", "", accession),
    point_label = paste0(Organism, "\n", genome)
  ) %>%
  select(Organism, genome, point_label, species, accession,
         mean_treated_sf, median_treated_sf,
         sd_sf, mad_sf, half_range_sf,
         meta_pvalue, neg_log10_meta_p, sd_neg_log10_p,
         fisher_p, neg_log10_fisher_p,
         stall_site_rank, n_reps_passing, any_hit)

resist_level <- merged %>%
  group_by(Organism) %>%
  summarise(
    mean_resist = mean(norm_perc_resistance),
    sd_resist   = sd(norm_perc_resistance),
    .groups = "drop"
  )

summary_df <- peak_level %>% left_join(resist_level, by = "Organism")

summary_df
```

## 6. Correlations

Correlations are computed at the organism level, on `summary_df`, not on the 18
raw replicate rows. There are 9 organisms; each contributes 2 Cy5 replicates,
and those two rows are repeated measurements of the same organism rather than
independent observations of the sf-vs-resistance relationship. Treating them as
independent inflates n from 9 to 18 and makes the correlation p-value too
small. For mean sf: r = 0.77, p = 1.9e-04 on 18 rows versus r = 0.80,
p = 9.2e-03 on 9 organisms. The correlation is slightly stronger when
aggregated; it is the p-value that changes materially.

```{r correlations}
merged <- merged %>% mutate(neg_log10_meta_p = -log10(meta_pvalue))

cor_at_organism_level <- function(x_var, method) {
  cor.test(summary_df[[x_var]], summary_df$mean_resist, method = method)
}

ct_mean_sf   <- cor_at_organism_level("mean_treated_sf",   "pearson")
ct_median_sf <- cor_at_organism_level("median_treated_sf", "pearson")
ct_metap     <- cor_at_organism_level("neg_log10_meta_p",  "spearman")

# Spearman on the sf axes too, for comparison across panels.
rho_mean_sf <- cor_at_organism_level("mean_treated_sf", "spearman")

make_cor_label <- function(ct) {
  stat <- if (ct$method == "Pearson's product-moment correlation") {
    paste0("Pearson r = ", round(unname(ct$estimate), 3))
  } else {
    paste0("Spearman rho = ", round(unname(ct$estimate), 3))
  }
  paste0(stat,
         "\np = ", signif(ct$p.value, 3),
         "\nn = ", nrow(summary_df), " organisms")
}

ct_mean_sf
ct_metap
rho_mean_sf
```

Spearman rho is 0.75 against mean sf, median sf and `-log10(meta p)` alike,
because all three put the nine organisms in the same order. Any difference
between the panels' Pearson r values reflects the shape of the x axis, not
additional information about the correlation.

## 7. Plot

One plotting function is used for both panels so the two versions differ only
in which variable is on the x axis and which is mapped to color.

```{r plot-function}
# x_var / x_err: columns in summary_df for the x position and its half-width
# color_var:     column in summary_df mapped to point color
# show_fit = FALSE drops the least-squares line, for an x variable where a
# linear fit is not meaningful (e.g. -log10(p); see 8a).
plot_resistance <- function(x_var, x_err, color_var,
                            x_lab, color_lab, title, subtitle,
                            cor_label, color_option = "plasma",
                            show_fit = TRUE) {

  fit_layer <- if (show_fit) {
    # Fit on the 9 organism means, matching the reported correlation, rather
    # than on the 18 replicate rows.
    geom_smooth(
      data = summary_df,
      aes(x = .data[[x_var]], y = mean_resist),
      method = "lm",            # "loess" for a curved fit
      se = TRUE,
      color = "grey20",
      fill = "steelblue",
      alpha = 0.15,
      linewidth = 0.7
    )
  } else {
    NULL
  }

  ggplot() +

    fit_layer +

    # raw replicate points, faded, to show the underlying spread
    geom_point(
      data = merged,
      aes(x = .data[[x_var]], y = norm_perc_resistance),
      color = "grey60", size = 1.6, alpha = 0.5
    ) +

    # horizontal error bars: spread of the 3 replicate measurements
    geom_errorbarh(
      data = summary_df,
      aes(y = mean_resist,
          xmin = .data[[x_var]] - .data[[x_err]],
          xmax = .data[[x_var]] + .data[[x_err]]),
      height = 0.02, color = "grey40"
    ) +

    # vertical error bars: spread of the 2 Cy5 resistance replicates
    geom_errorbar(
      data = summary_df,
      aes(x = .data[[x_var]],
          ymin = mean_resist - sd_resist,
          ymax = mean_resist + sd_resist),
      width = 0.015 * diff(range(summary_df[[x_var]])),
      color = "grey40"
    ) +

    geom_point(
      data = summary_df,
      aes(x = .data[[x_var]], y = mean_resist, color = .data[[color_var]]),
      size = 4.5
    ) +

    scale_color_viridis_c(name = color_lab, option = color_option) +

    # label = organism name + genome accession, on two lines
    geom_text_repel(
      data = summary_df,
      aes(x = .data[[x_var]], y = mean_resist, label = point_label),
      size = 3.0, lineheight = 0.9, color = "grey20",
      box.padding = 0.5, point.padding = 0.3,
      min.segment.length = 0, segment.color = "grey70",
      max.overlaps = Inf
    ) +

    annotate(
      "text",
      x = min(merged[[x_var]]) + 0.02 * diff(range(merged[[x_var]])),
      y = max(merged$norm_perc_resistance) * 0.98,
      label = cor_label,
      hjust = 0, vjust = 1, size = 3.6, fontface = "italic"
    ) +

    labs(x = x_lab, y = "Normalized % Resistance",
         title = title, subtitle = subtitle) +
    theme_minimal(base_size = 12) +
    theme(
      panel.grid.minor = element_blank(),
      plot.title = element_text(face = "bold")
    )
}
```

x = updated mean stall fraction, colored by meta p-value. This is the only
figure the notebook produces; section 8 documents the checks behind it.

```{r plot-sf, fig.width=8.5, fig.height=6.5, warning=FALSE, message=FALSE}
p_sf <- plot_resistance(
  x_var     = "mean_treated_sf",
  x_err     = "sd_sf",
  color_var = "neg_log10_meta_p",
  x_lab     = "Mean treated stall fraction (261019 re-run)",
  color_lab = expression(-log[10]("meta p-value")),
  title     = "Normalized % Resistance vs mean stall fraction",
  subtitle  = paste(
    "Horiz. error = SD of 3 sf replicates; vert. error = SD of 2 Cy5",
    "resistance replicates;\ncolor = meta p-value from the re-run;",
    "fit and correlation on the 9 organism means"
  ),
  cor_label = make_cor_label(ct_mean_sf)
)

p_sf
```

## 8. Diagnostics

None of these produce a figure. Each one documents a check behind the single
plot above.

### 8a. Does the choice of summary variable change the result?

It does not. All three candidate x variables put the nine organisms in the same
order, so Spearman rho is identical for all three, and the Pearson r values
differ only by a few thousandths. This is the reason the notebook produces one
figure rather than three: a second panel reporting the same rank statistic
would invite a reader to compare Pearson r values across differently shaped x
axes, which is not a valid comparison.

`-log10(meta p)` is reported with Spearman only. It is not a measurement but
the output of the stall-calling test, and it depends on read depth as well as
effect size, so a least-squares fit to it would stack one inference on another.

```{r ranking-variable-check}
ranking_check <- bind_rows(
  data.frame(
    x_variable = "mean sf",
    pearson_r  = unname(ct_mean_sf$estimate),
    pearson_p  = ct_mean_sf$p.value,
    spearman_rho = unname(rho_mean_sf$estimate),
    spearman_p   = rho_mean_sf$p.value
  ),
  data.frame(
    x_variable = "median sf",
    pearson_r  = unname(ct_median_sf$estimate),
    pearson_p  = ct_median_sf$p.value,
    spearman_rho = unname(
      cor_at_organism_level("median_treated_sf", "spearman")$estimate),
    spearman_p   =
      cor_at_organism_level("median_treated_sf", "spearman")$p.value
  ),
  data.frame(
    x_variable = "-log10(meta p)",
    pearson_r  = NA_real_,   # not reported: see note above
    pearson_p  = NA_real_,
    spearman_rho = unname(ct_metap$estimate),
    spearman_p   = ct_metap$p.value
  )
)

ranking_check
```

Per-organism ranks under each variable, to confirm nothing moves:

```{r rank-compare}
summary_df %>%
  mutate(
    rank_mean_sf   = rank(-mean_treated_sf),
    rank_median_sf = rank(-median_treated_sf),
    rank_metap     = rank(-neg_log10_meta_p)
  ) %>%
  arrange(rank_mean_sf) %>%
  select(Organism, genome, mean_treated_sf, median_treated_sf,
         neg_log10_meta_p, rank_mean_sf, rank_median_sf, rank_metap)
```

### 8b. Replicate R3 is systematically the lowest

R3 is the lowest of the three sf replicates for all nine organisms. This does
not affect the correlation, but it is a systematic property of the sequencing
replicates rather than noise, and worth knowing independently of this figure.
It is also why the mean is used rather than the median: with n = 3 the median
discards R3 every time, so it is not a robust summary here but the midpoint of
R1 and R2 with a consistently lower third replicate dropped.

```{r r3-check}
summary_df %>%
  left_join(
    merged %>% distinct(Organism, treated_sf_R1, treated_sf_R2, treated_sf_R3),
    by = "Organism"
  ) %>%
  mutate(lowest_rep = c("R1", "R2", "R3")[
    apply(cbind(treated_sf_R1, treated_sf_R2, treated_sf_R3), 1, which.min)
  ]) %>%
  arrange(desc(mean_treated_sf)) %>%
  select(Organism, treated_sf_R1, treated_sf_R2, treated_sf_R3,
         lowest_rep, mean_treated_sf, median_treated_sf)
```

### 8c. Spread statistics

Error bars use SD. MAD is tabled only to show why it is not used: at n = 3 one
of the three absolute deviations from the median is exactly zero, so
`median(|x - median(x)|)` returns the smaller of the two non-zero deviations
and collapses toward zero when the replicates are asymmetric. For `pesti` the
three sf values span 0.074 and MAD returns 0.0012. SD and half-range track each
other; MAD tracks neither.

```{r spread-compare}
summary_df %>%
  mutate(mad_over_sd = mad_sf / sd_sf) %>%
  arrange(desc(mean_treated_sf)) %>%
  select(Organism, sd_sf, half_range_sf, mad_sf, mad_over_sd)
```

### 8d. meta p-value vs Fisher recombination

Cross-check on the re-run's own replicate combination. These should track each
other closely; large disagreement means the re-run combines replicates
differently from a plain Fisher combination of the three per-replicate
p-values, which would matter before quoting `meta_pvalue` anywhere.

```{r p-crosscheck}
summary_df %>%
  mutate(difference = neg_log10_meta_p - neg_log10_fisher_p) %>%
  arrange(desc(neg_log10_meta_p)) %>%
  select(Organism, genome, meta_pvalue, fisher_p,
         neg_log10_meta_p, neg_log10_fisher_p, difference)
```

## 9. The second Zika genome

The assay library contains two Zika references. Only `NC_035889.1` has a Cy5
quantification, because that is the accession the tested tile came from, so
only that one is plotted above. The block below reports the best tile on the
other genome for comparison, without adding it to the figure. Copying the
`NC_035889.1` resistance value onto it would be fabricated data, and it would
also pull the fit, since the two points would sit at the same y with different
x.

```{r zika-second}
zika_species <- "Orthoflavivirus zikaense"

zika_best <- peaks_all %>%
  filter(species == zika_species) %>%
  mutate(genome = sub("\\|.*$", "", accession)) %>%
  group_by(genome) %>%
  slice_min(meta_pvalue, n = 1, with_ties = FALSE) %>%
  ungroup() %>%
  mutate(neg_log10_meta_p = -log10(meta_pvalue)) %>%
  select(genome, peak_id, tile_id, meta_pvalue, neg_log10_meta_p,
         mean_treated_sf, stall_site_rank, n_reps_passing, any_hit) %>%
  arrange(meta_pvalue)

zika_best
```

If the second genome should still appear as a reference line rather than a
data point, this adds it to the figure without implying a resistance
measurement. The line sits at that tile's mean stall fraction:

```{r zika-second-annotation, fig.width=8.5, fig.height=6.5, warning=FALSE, message=FALSE}
zika_other <- zika_best %>%
  filter(genome != "NC_035889.1") %>%
  slice(1)

p_sf_annot <- p_sf +
  geom_vline(
    xintercept = zika_other$mean_treated_sf,
    linetype = "dashed", color = "grey50", linewidth = 0.5
  ) +
  annotate(
    "text",
    x = zika_other$mean_treated_sf,
    y = min(merged$norm_perc_resistance),
    label = paste0("zikv ", zika_other$genome, " best tile\n(no Cy5 quant)"),
    hjust = -0.05, vjust = 0, size = 3, color = "grey40"
  )

p_sf_annot
```

## 10. Save to file

```{r save}
save_all <- function(plot, stem, width = 8.5, height = 6.5) {
  ggsave(paste0(stem, ".png"), plot, width = width, height = height, dpi = 300)
  ggsave(paste0(stem, ".pdf"), plot, width = width, height = height)
  ggsave(paste0(stem, ".svg"), plot, width = width, height = height)
}

save_all(p_sf, "resistance_vs_mean_sf_20261105")
```

SVG export requires the `svglite` package; PNG and PDF need no extra package.
